column1: # Your AI subscriptions' own tools: the "who answers" pickers (Terminal, Chat, the Code page's terminal panel) and
# Settings › Claude Code › Your AI subscriptions read this table (portal/portal/answers.py). Each tool is its provider's
# own, unmodified client in the sandbox's image (terminal/Dockerfile's ai-tools stage), signed in there with its own
# flow; the sandbox's terminal/bin/subscriptions has the same ids (tests/test_subscriptions.sh checks both lists).
# id  name  provider  plan  command  signout  chat_model  chat_why  terms
#   plan        whose plan it uses, in a few words
#   command     what to type in the sandbox's terminal
#   signout     cli: it has a sign-out command (Settings' Sign out runs it) | inside: only inside its own screen (said)
#   chat_model  yes: a model in Open WebUI's list (plan-<id>, the code container's connection) while it is signed in; no: greyed,
#               with chat_why — chat_why says how and under which of the provider's terms. The tool itself opens in Chat either way
#   terms       the provider's page this rests on

column4: your Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise)
column8: A Chat model on your Claude plan's limits, through the Claude Agent SDK — the same Claude Code, with no tool — behind Settings' switch (off by default): Anthropic's support article allows the SDK on a plan; its legal page says other apps may not route requests through a Free, Pro or Max plan on their users' behalf.

A Chat model on your ChatGPT plan, through Codex's own app server (the interface OpenAI's own extensions use), in Chat's own sandbox, without its tools (no shell, no MCP server, no web search): it answers, it runs nothing. OpenAI's Sign in with ChatGPT terms for other apps ask that requests come from your own runtime and not serve as general API access.

column4: an organisation's Gemini Code Assist, or your own Gemini API key
column8: Google's subscriptions no longer work in Gemini CLI (since 2026-06-18): Gemini in Chat is planned through your own Gemini API key. Gemini CLI itself opens here with an organisation's Code Assist login or your key.

A Chat model on your Copilot plan, through Copilot CLI's ACP mode (in public preview; GitHub documents it for other apps): in Chat's own sandbox, its tools switched off; a tool it reaches for anyway stops its answer.
A Chat model on your Cursor plan, through Cursor CLI's ACP mode in its ask mode (questions and answers, read only); in Chat's own sandbox; a tool it reaches for stops its answer.

A Chat model on your SuperGrok or X plan, through Grok Build's ACP mode (xAI documents it for headless use; its acceptable use policy rules out unauthorized automated means — here you ask, it answers); in Chat's own sandbox, its tools switched off; a tool it reaches for anyway stops its answer.
